references.text: God elaborates on the meaning of 'I AM' (אֶהְיֶה) that He mentioned in verse 12 and reveals His name to Moses.
God repeats the promise to be with Moses (אֶהְיֶה עִם־פִּיךָ), the same expression found in 3:12.
The fulfillment of the sign: Israel comes to Mount Sinai to serve God, just as promised in 3:12.
The people worship God on the mountain, which is the final fulfillment of the sign given to Moses.
God uses the same promise to Isaac: 'I am with you' (אָנֹכִי אִתְּךָ), a recurring theme in the patriarchal narratives.
God promises Jacob 'I am with you' (אָנֹכִי עִמָּךְ), the same promise given to Moses.
God gives the same promise to Joshua as He gave to Moses: 'I will be with you' (אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ).
God promises Gideon 'I will be with you' (אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ), the same assurance Moses received.
Isaiah speaks of a sign (אוֹת) from God, similar to the concept of the sign given to Moses.
God promises Jeremiah 'I am with you' (כִּי־אִתְּךָ אָנִי), the same promise given to Moses at his calling.
Jesus promises the disciples 'I am with you all days' (ἐγὼ μεθʼ ὑμῶν εἰμι), a parallel to God's promise to Moses.
Stephen quotes this promise in his speech that the people will serve God at this place (λατρεύσουσίν μοι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ τούτῳ).
Both verses link the promise of God's presence and identity ('I will be your God') directly to the event of the Exodus from Egypt.
Acts 7:34 is a direct retelling of the event in Exodus 3, where God explains His motivation and gives the mission to Moses.
Both verses show God's presence ('I will be with you') as a guarantee of fearlessness in connection with travels to and from Egypt.
Jeremiah explicitly quoted the covenant formula from the books of Exodus and linked it to the exodus from Egypt to remind the people of their obligations.
